result:
The proposed answer is not supported, so I reject it.

The solution's central step is unjustified. Borel–Serre duality relates the top cohomology of $\Gamma_{0,3}^+(p)\subset \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ to Steinberg-type homology of the boundary of the symmetric space, which is 3-dimensional for $\mathrm{SL}_3$. It does not identify $H^3$ with weight-2 cusp forms for $\Gamma_0(p)\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, which govern a different group and a different degree. The claimed isomorphism is asserted without justification.

The genus claim is also wrong on its own terms. The genus of $X_0(p)$ is 0 for $p=2,3,5,7,13$, not just $2,3,5,7$. Even if the reduction to genus were valid, the set would include 13, and the sum would not be 17. Also, $X_0(11)$ has genus 1, so "vanishes precisely for $p=2,3,5,7$" is false as stated.

I could not verify the correct finite set from memory. The relevant results are in work of Miller, Patzt and Putman on top-dimensional cohomology of congruence subgroups, but I am not certain of the exact list, so I am not giving a replacement answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
